title: Staged release circuit breaker and observation scratchpad
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working scratchpad for a small-team playbook that layers a circuit-breaker and observation ritual on top of staged releases (canary, small-ramp A/B). The goal is not to invent another gating doc but to capture pragmatic, operational-ready heuristics we can iterate on in the next two sprints. This doc is intentionally informal: quick notes, experiments to try, and TODOs.

Why this exists (hypothesis):
- Even with good slice selection, LLM releases have failure modes that are only visible at edge and cost surfaces (token blowups, function-call regressions, silent hallucinations).
- We need a low-latency automatic containment mechanism (circuit-breaker) plus an ops checklist so humans can decide rollback vs remediation.

Key concepts (working definitions):
- Soft-breaker: automated traffic throttles or model-fallback when intermediate signals degrade (e.g., p99 latency spikes by >2x or hallucination-score increases beyond threshold).
- Hard-breaker: immediate traffic cut and revert to last-stable variant (trigger requiring oncall escalation).
- Observation window: 15m rolling window by default; longer (1h) for long-tail tests.
- Exposure profile: micro-slice (0.1%–1%), small-ramp (1%–10%), broad (>=10%).

Signals to monitor (prioritized):
1) Latency (p50, p95, p99) by route and model variant. Token-level tail matters for chat context-heavy flows.
2) Cost delta (cost / 1000 tokens or embeddings) — abrupt cost regressions might indicate new model size/quantization mismatch.
3) Functional integrity (for function-calling flows): failed tool calls / invalid JSON / output-schema-violations.
4) Semantic quality proxies: unexpected increases in fallback prompts, increased user edits, negative satisfaction reactions (if available).
5) Safety flags / moderation hits / hallucination heuristic (our evals infra emits a 'hallucination-score').
6) Error rate (HTTP 5xx, timeouts, kernel OOMs).
7) Synthetic traffic pass/fail (see harness below).

Circuit-breaker mechanics (proposal):
- Two-tier triggers: soft trigger -> reduce exposure by factor of 5 (e.g., 1% -> 0.2%); hard trigger -> immediate switch to pinned-stable model and page oncall.
- Soft trigger logic (any of): latency p99 > baseline*2 for 15m, function-failure-rate > baseline + 0.5%, hallucination-score increase > 0.25 absolute.
- Hard trigger logic (any of): p99 > baseline*3 for 5m, error-rate > 3% for 5m, safety-moderation spike > x10 baseline.

Example traffic orchestration pseudocode (informal):
- if soft_trigger: set_exposure(current_slice, max(0.001, exposure/5))
- if hard_trigger: route_all_to(stable_variant); create_incident(TAG:rollout-hard-breaker)

Synthetic canary harness (what to run pre-exposure and continuously during exposure):
- Replay top-50 production queries (anonymized) against new variant and baseline; diff token-gen, function-calls, latency.
- Run 1000 synthetic long-context chains to exercise kv-cache and memory behavior.
- Reranker/Ranking-specific: run top-10 pairwise tests to detect ordering flips and logging of divergence types.

Observation ritual (human + automated):
- 0–15m after exposure: automated signal sweep run; if any soft-trigger -> reduce exposure and notify channel (#rollouts-observe).
- 15–60m: oncall joins, review synth diffs, sample real user sessions (3–5), decide to progress or revert.
- Post-rollback: short RCA stub within 24h and gating changes for next attempt.

Escalation and comms template (quick):
- Automated: "[AUTO] Soft-breaker triggered for rollout R1234: p99 latency +120%. Exposure reduced 1%->0.2%. Next steps: oncall review within 30m."
- Human: "Hard-breaker activated for R1234: routing reverted to stable@v12. Pager: @oncall. Postmortem owner assigned: product-hosted-api."

Open questions / TODOs:
- What should baseline be for hallucination-score? Rolling 7-day median? TODO: ask research (ENG-5029).
- How to instrument cost-per-1000 tokens with mixed quantization profiles? (engineering: infra-telemetry).
- Should soft-breaker actions be reversible automatically when signals normalize? Pro: reduces toil. Con: oscillation risk. Proposed: require normalization for 30m continuous before auto-increase.
- Ops UX: do we surface breaker actions in Console with a one-click 're-run canary' button? Product to prototype.

Playbook checklist (short):
- Pre-launch: synth harness green, monitoring alerts created, runbook pinned, oncall notified, rollback tag ready.
- Launch minute 0: monitor synth and p95, confirm telemetry is arriving.
- Launch minute 15: decision point; escalate if signals not nominal.

Quick notes from experiments (lab):
- 2025-01-30: ran long-context synth (1k tokens) and observed 18% more KV eviction churn on quantized variant; soft-breaker would have triggered at p99>2x baseline.
- 2025-02-14: reranker edge-case: ordering flip caused 2% absolute conversion drop on toy slice. Need precomputed pairwise sanity tests.

Next steps (this doc owner):
- Wire-up synthetic harness (PR link above) to run automatically pre-exposure and during exposure. Owner: Evelyn.
- Draft Console UI mock for breaker visibility and manual override. Owner: Priya.
- Create alerting rules in prod monitoring (SLO-backed thresholds). Owner: SRE (ENG-5022).

Notes-to-self: keep this doc short-lived; move validated patterns into canonical rollout runbook (Confluence) once we have concrete thresholds and tooling.

References and links: see linked_artifacts above. Also: quick sketch in GH PR 27 has a toy implementation of soft-throttle logic for testing.

-- Marcos
